text: Get-AzVM and Stop-AzVM each act on one resource at a time by default, the way every cmdlet from the Az module did in Lesson 5. That's fine for a single VM typed at a console, but it breaks down fast once a subscription has fifteen VMs and you need to know which are running, or stop all of them before a maintenance window. The fix isn't fifteen separate commands typed one after another — it's a loop that runs the same logic once per resource, automatically, without you retyping anything.

Get-AzVM with no arguments returns every VM in the current subscription as a collection, all at once. A foreach statement walks that collection one item at a time: foreach ($vm in $vms) runs its block once per VM in the collection, and inside the block $vm holds that particular pass's VM object, with the same Name, ResourceGroupName, and other properties any single Get-AzVM result would have had on its own.

PowerShell's pipeline offers a second way to loop: piping Get-AzVM straight into ForEach-Object, where $_ plays the same role $vm did above. Get-AzVM -Status also adds a PowerState property to each VM it returns — VM running, VM stopped, or VM deallocated. Piping that into ForEach-Object and wrapping each result in a PSCustomObject builds a clean report, one row per VM, with exactly the Name, ResourceGroup, and PowerState columns asked for, instead of the full raw object.

Looping gets more useful once it's combined with filtering first. Where-Object narrows Get-AzVM's output down to just the VMs tagged Environment equals Dev before the loop ever runs, and ForEach-Object then stops each one that matched — the exact pattern Chapter 6 builds a full cost-savings script around later in this course. -Force skips the confirmation prompt Stop-AzVM would otherwise show for every VM, and -NoWait submits each stop request without waiting on the previous one to finish first.

Next: PowerShell functions for reusable automation — wrapping this exact filter-then-loop pattern in a function with its own name and parameters, so it can be called by name from other scripts instead of retyped by hand every single time it's needed.
